text.p: The supervisory board of Daimler-Benz AG is on January 23 expected to approve a proposal to merge Daimler with its car unit Mercedes-Benz AG, effective January 1 1997, sources at the company said Saturday.
Once the restructure takes place, Daimler's newly formed management board would not include a post carrying responsibility for the Mercedes group alone, the sources said.
The sources were confirming a report this weekend in the Spiegel magazine, which said a decision had finally been reached on the future status of Mercedes in the Daimler group.
Spiegel had also said that Hilmar Kopper, who heads Daimler's supervisory board, and Karl Feuerstein, head of Daimler's works council, had indicated they approved the move.

The magazine also said that Mercedes future representation on the Daimler-Benz management board would comprise representatives of its car division, its commercial division and its distribution department.
It was unclear whether the current chief excecutive of Mercedes-Benz, Helmut Werner, would remain in the company, Spiegel said. Werner had opposed the merger plans.
Daimler has been debating a new management structure for several months, as its chief executive Juergen Schrempp attempts to forge a more streamlined organisation.
Since his takeover at the helm of Daimler in May 1995, the group has given up 11 of the 35 business divisions it once controlled.
